# A year’s end

A cycle’s real first and last days, where it stands on a day, and the week its results are judged at: the clock, not a button, ends a year.

## The rule

**A cycle's days.** Week 0 is the week before week 1 (for starting numbers). A cycle's **first day** is week 1's Monday (`startDate` + 7 days); its **last day** is its last week's Sunday (`startDate` + (`weeks` + 1) × 7 − 1 days). The wrap-up **opens** on the Monday of week `weeks − 2 + 1` (its last 2 weeks) and **closes** 4 weeks after the last day.

**Where it stands** on a day (`cycleState`): `before` its first day (week 0 included); `running` until the day before the wrap-up opens; `ending` until its last day; `ended` until the wrap-up closes; `closed` after. The clock decides, never a button: a year ends on its last day whether or not anyone starts the next. The frame says it in one line (`placeLine`): "2026 · week 46 · Q4"; "2026 · week 53, the last week"; "2026 has ended"; before week 1, "2027 starts Mon 4 Jan 2027".

**The week results are judged at** (`resultWeek`) is the week by the calendar, held to 0…`weeks + 1`: the current week until the last day, then `weeks + 1`. A goal's result, its quarters and the last quarter's close read it, so a goal due in the last week gets its result, and Q4 closes on the numbers there are, the day after the year ends. Everything else keeps `currentWeek`, which stops at the last week: a check-in given after the end is dated the last week.

**After the last day nothing in the cycle is due, late or out of date.** No check-in is due (no "due" flag, nothing on Home's check-in block), and no goal becomes "No recent update" for want of a check-in: each keeps the last status its owner gave.

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| The demo’s 2026: week 0 from Monday 22 December 2025, 53 weeks. Its days. | `first 2025-12-29, last 2027-01-03, wrap-up 2026-12-21 to 2027-01-31` |
| 2027 (week 0 from Monday 28 December 2026, 52 weeks). | `first 2027-01-04, last 2028-01-02, wrap-up 2027-12-20 to 2028-01-30` |
| 2026 on Sunday 20 December 2026, Monday 21 December, Monday 28 December, Monday 4 January 2027 and Monday 1 February 2027: its state, and the frame. | `running 2026 · week 51 · Q4 / ending 2026 · week 52 · Q4 / ending 2026 · week 53, the last week / ended 2026 has ended / closed 2026 has ended` |
| Is 2026’s wrap-up open on Sunday 20 December 2026, Monday 21 December, Sunday 31 January 2027 and Monday 1 February 2027? | `no, yes, yes, no` |
| 2027 seen on Monday 21 December 2026, before its week 1. | `2027 starts Mon 4 Jan 2027` |
| A 13-week cycle from Monday 28 September 2026 (week 0). | `first 2026-10-05, last 2027-01-03, wrap-up opens 2026-12-21` |
| The week and the week results are judged at, on Sunday 3 January 2027 and Monday 4 January 2027, in 2026. | `53 53 / 53 54` |
| G-37, 4 → 40 pairs due in week 53 of 2026, with 33 pairs in week 53. Its result and Q4 on Sunday 3 January 2027, then on Monday 4 January. | `none, Q4: plan 40 pairs by week 53 / Not met: due week 53, Q4: 33 pairs against a plan of 40 pairs, 7 pairs short` |
| The same goal with its last check-in in week 46 (posted 11 November 2026): its status, and whether its check-in is due, on Sunday 3 January 2027 and on Monday 11 January. | `No recent update, due / On track, not due` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** How long the wrap-up stays open after the year ends (four weeks) and how early it opens (two weeks) are choices, kept in RULES; the rebuild may tune them.

## Where it lives

- [src/domain/cycle.ts](../../../src/domain/cycle.ts): `cycleDates`, `cycleState`, `wrapUpOpenOn`, `wrapUpOpen`, `wrapUpCycle`, `placeLine`, `periodNow`, `dayWithYear`
- [src/domain/plan.ts](../../../src/domain/plan.ts): `resultWeek`, `hasEnded`
- [src/domain/thresholds.ts](../../../src/domain/thresholds.ts): `RULES`

## Requirements

- `RESULTS`: A cycle ends on its last day (its last week's Sunday) whether or not the next is started: results and the last quarter close on the numbers there are, and nothing in it is due, late or out of date afterwards. Every place that says where the year stands gives its real first and last days: running, ending (the wrap-up's weeks), ended or not begun.
- `YEAR`: Goals are set for the year: a goal year starting in the month each workspace picks, in four quarters. Quarter targets, and any week in between, are read off the owner’s own plan; each ended quarter shows met or missed against it, a missed quarter is flagged in the goal’s story, and history can be seen for this quarter or the whole year.
